caption_used: The character distribution in RoleplayPref is organized into three primary categories — Virtual Characters, Custom Characters, and Real Characters — with 13 subcategories in the outer ring. Virtual Characters occupy approximately 60% of the distribution and are subdivided into Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters, with Movie Characters forming the largest virtual subcategory. Real Characters comprise seven subcategories including Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers, with Musicians representing the largest real-character segment. Custom Characters occupy a small portion with no labeled subcategories.

raw_responses.Bulgarian: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a donut chart illustrating the distribution of characters in RoleplayPref, categorized into three primary groups: Virtual Characters, Custom Characters, and Real Characters, with 13 subcategories in the outer ring. The central blue ring represents Virtual Characters, which occupy approximately 60% of the chart and are subdivided into five subcategories: Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters, all displayed in light blue shades. The outer ring is divided into two sections: Real Characters, shown in green shades, and Custom Characters, shown in pink. Real Characters include seven subcategories—Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers—each represented by a distinct segment in the green section, with Musicians being the largest among them. Custom Characters are represented by a single pink segment with no labeled subcategories. The chart includes labels for each subcategory, and the segments are arranged in a circular layout with no visual emphasis such as expansion or highlighting. There is no separate legend, as all categories and subcategories are directly labeled on the chart.
raw_responses.English: DESCRIPTION: The chart is a donut-style pie chart illustrating the distribution of characters in RoleplayPref, organized into three primary categories: Virtual Characters, Custom Characters, and Real Characters, with 13 subcategories represented in the outer ring. The largest segment, Virtual Characters, occupies approximately 60% of the chart and is subdivided into five subcategories: Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters, with Movie Characters being the largest individual subcategory within this group. The Real Characters category includes seven subcategories — Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers — with Musicians being the largest within this group. Custom Characters form a smaller, unlabeled segment. The chart uses distinct colors for each category and subcategory, with labels placed adjacent to or inside the corresponding slices. The outer ring segments are arranged in a clockwise order, with the largest subcategories positioned toward the top-right of the chart. The inner ring highlights the three main categories, with Virtual Characters in a medium blue, Real Characters in green, and Custom Characters in red. No slices are exploded or emphasized beyond their size and color differentiation.
raw_responses.German: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a radial chart illustrating the distribution of characters in the RoleplayPref dataset, organized into three primary categories—Virtual Characters, Custom Characters, and Real Characters—each represented as a distinct segment in the inner ring. The outer ring further subdivides these categories into 13 subcategories. Virtual Characters, shown in a light blue segment, constitute approximately 60% of the total distribution and are subdivided into Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters. Among these, Movie Characters form the largest subcategory within Virtual Characters. Real Characters, represented in green, make up a smaller portion of the distribution and include Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers, with Musicians being the largest subcategory in this group. Custom Characters, depicted in red, occupy a small segment with no labeled subcategories. The chart includes labels for each subcategory positioned around the outer edge, with no explicit percentage values inside the segments, and no visual emphasis such as highlighting or separation of segments. The arrangement of subcategories appears to follow a clockwise sequence around the ring.
